recently moved to this general practice and I regret moving at all. I’d prefer the 40 minute drive to my previous GPs over the below woeful experiences the last several weeks.

Attached image of a confirmation text from the GPs. Booked the morning off work, arrive to the appointment to be told I’m booked in for September. Today is Friday the 15th August. Not Monday the 15th September.

Secondly, advised over the phone to register my daughter for the GPs I’ll need to come physically into the building to scan a QR code that isn’t on the website. Scanned, completed and registered. Popped in to see if this has progressed as we’ve heard nothing - nothing on the system, come in with your child to register her. Another morning off work.

Finally, the biggest disaster - I’ve had a kidney stone for several weeks, agonising pain. Hospital discharged me with a scan booked that due to a motorway accident I couldn’t attend (things happen, life…). I ended up back in hospital again with kidney pain and was advised to raise with my GP to rebook a scan, raised via patches and requested “update via telephone” (though I’m not sure why you’d bother given they’ll either just update in patches with no notification to you or text, they don’t honour the requested means of contact). No update for a week, I log into patches to find the request has been cancelled due to “more information required” from the GP. Bear in mind the request outlines a doctor at the hospital has outlined I require a kidney scan and to request this from the GPs. Symptoms = kidney pain likely stones (not confirmed yet as need the scan, could be more malicious!) and noted worsening pain.

I raise another patches request and am advised to come in later that week. At this point I’ve no more tramadol a new born baby and I can’t move. I’ve rang the GP to ask for help, they advised ring 111, I ring 111 who advise speak to the GP. 111 ring the GP who advise they can’t see me today, so I end up back in hospital. With agonising pain.

Avoid entirely. I’ll be moving myself, my partner and our child to another GPs that doesn’t have such shocking reviews. And I can see why. One gentleman behind the reception counter is genuinely lovely and helpful, one male doctor (with a slight lisp, apologies on the description but credit due where credit is due his expertise and professionalism were exceptional and I don’t know his name!) the rest of the staff that I have encountered should take note of the above as my experiences have been of incompetence, unhelpful, rude, demeaning and frustrated tones over the phone. Almost as though it’s somehow MY fault information isn’t being passed between health care “professionals” via hospital > GP and / or completed forms disappearing into the void.
